A gift from Nagash to a loyal servant, the Hungering Blade will prolong the unholy existence of its wielder should he ever be in peril.
To be honest, it is mostly executioner. Everyone who stands against Nagash is guilty by default.

No land is too remote – no place truly out of reach.
Magic made the Hand what he is now, but in war he prefers cold steel to sorcery.
Burn the cities of the living so they may join us in death.
In the name of Nagash, all kingdoms must fall. There is no rest, no peace, and no mercy.

Gunther Larenscheld has awoken one of Nagash's most loyal lieutenants, the Dread King, in exchange for eternal life. Now he has received the promised reward – even in death, his spirit will not leave the mortal world.
Freed from the limitations of a body, Larenscheld is a far more capable fighter in death than he ever was in life.
Larenscheld's ghost haunts the living, stalking the soldiers of his enemies.
Larenscheld specialises in killing the greatest of foes, extinguishing their potent life force in the name of Nagash.
Nagash allows Larenscheld's spirit to channel the Winds of Magic, enabling him to cast spells even in his ghost form.
Master of the dead in life – still master of the dead in death.
Larenscheld opens a portal through which vengeful spirits in the form of ethereal skulls pour forth, crashing down upon the living and wreaking devastation.
The hardship endured to achieve immortality makes Larenscheld cling to his unlife with an iron will forged by desperation and suffering.
Larenscheld may shed his mortal form at any time, assuming his superior ghostly aspect.
No longer a mere apparition, Larenscheld's will endures beyond death – and grows ever more powerful.
Luthor is Larenscheld's faithful servant. He excels at ambush and subterfuge, disposing of meddlesome adventurers and shielding his master from daggers in the dark.
The liche has forsaken life to attain existence as an immortal undead. So long as its will remains unbroken, it is almost impossible to destroy permanently.
